title: Male Body Surface Anatomy: Anterior Landmarks & Regions
description: Study male body surface anatomy in standard anatomical position, connecting anterior bony landmarks, muscle contours, and body wall regions to deep organs.
h1: Male Body Surface Anatomy: Anterior Landmarks and Underlying Organs
blurb: Standard anatomical position on the anterior male figure: palpable bony landmarks, muscular contours, and body-wall regions mapped to underlying internal viscera.
lead: Before looking inside any single organ system, anatomists read the body from the outside in—using visible bony ridges and muscular contours as a map to deeper structures. In this illustrated guide to male body surface anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including brain, thyroid gland, lungs, heart—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Before looking inside any single organ system, anatomists read the body from the outside in—using visible bony ridges and muscular contours as a map to deeper structures. Use this page as an orientation map: click any glowing organ to jump into its full entry with the realistic render, labelled schematic and quiz. Within the human body, the male body — anterior (Corpus masculinum) is situated in whole body — anterior view, receives arterial perfusion via systemic + pulmonary circuits, and is innervated by central + peripheral nervous systems.

The brain (Encephalon) control centre housed in the skull, glowing through the translucent scalp. Physiologically, the brain integrates sensation, movement, thought, memory and autonomic drive. Structurally, the thyroid gland (Glandula thyroidea) comprises butterfly-shaped gland on the front of the neck. Physiologically, the thyroid gland governs sets metabolic rate via T3/T4 under TSH control. The lungs (Pulmones) are paired thoracic organs flanking the heart. Physiologically, the lungs governs gas exchange across ~300 million alveoli. The heart (Cor) is muscular pump in the mediastinum, a little left of midline. Physiologically, the heart drives about 5 L of blood per minute through two circuits. Structurally, the liver (Hepar) comprises largest internal organ, right upper quadrant. Physiologically, the liver governs metabolism, detoxification, bile, plasma proteins. Structurally, the stomach (Gaster) comprises j-shaped reservoir under the diaphragm, left side. Physiologically, the stomach governs acid–pepsin digestion; intrinsic factor for B12.

Clinically, regarding the brain, stroke risk rises with age — remember FAST: face, arms, speech, time. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the thyroid gland, hypothyroidism causes fatigue, weight gain and cold intolerance. In clinical pathology involving the lungs, smoking destroys alveolar walls → emphysema. Medical evaluation of the heart also notes that coronary blockage causes myocardial infarction.

questions.question: Where are the main organs in the male body?
questions.answer: The brain is in the skull; heart and lungs are in the chest; liver, stomach, intestines and kidneys are in the abdomen; and the bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles and rectum are in the pelvis. The testes and penis are external genital structures.

questions.question: Which male structures need a deeper view than the body map?
questions.answer: The prostate, seminal vesicles, pelvic nerves and microscopic tissue layers require dedicated regional views; a whole-body plate is for orientation.

questions.question: Where is the brain shown on the male body map?
questions.answer: The male body map shows the brain in the head, enclosed by the skull.

questions.question: Where are the lungs in the male body map?
questions.answer: The male body map shows the lungs in the chest on either side of the heart.

questions.question: What liver details are shown on the male body map?
questions.answer: The whole-body view marks the liver as a major upper-abdominal organ but does not show lobes, vessels or segmental anatomy; see the liver chapter for those details.
